record.paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Creative Telescoping
record.context_brief: Reduction-based creative telescoping for D-finite functions
record.original_question: Develop a reduction-based creative telescoping algorithm for a given Fuchsian D-finite function f(x, y). The algorithm should compute, when possible, rational functions c_0(x), c_1(x), ..., c_r(x) in C(x), not all zero, and an operator Q in C(x, y)[D_x, D_y] such that (c_0 + c_1 D_x + ... + c_r D_x^r) · f = D_y Q · f.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2 Develop a reduction based creative telescoping algorithm which for a given (Fuchsian) D-finite function f(x, y) computes, if possible, rational functions c0, c1, ··· , cr ∈ C(x), not all zero, such that there exists an operator Q ∈ C(x, y)[Dx, Dy] with (c0 + c1Dx + ··· + crDr_x) · f = DyQ · f.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C$ be a field of characteristic zero (e.g., $\mathbb{Q}$ or $\mathbb{C}$), and let $f(x,y)$ be a Fuchsian D-finite function in two variables; that is, $f$ is annihilated by a nonzero linear differential operator in $C(x,y)[D_x,D_y]$ all of whose singularities (in the relevant variable, viewed as a univariate operator over $C(x,y)$ with respect to $D_y$) are regular (Fuchsian) with real exponents. Let $D_x = \partial/\partial x$ and $D_y = \partial/\partial y$.

Design an algorithm of "reduction-based" type (in the spirit of Hermite-style reductions, which compute telescopers without simultaneously constructing the certificate) that, given such an $f$, decides whether there exist rational functions $c_0(x), c_1(x), \dots, c_r(x) \in C(x)$, not all zero, and an operator $Q \in C(x,y)[D_x,D_y]$ such that
$$\bigl(c_0(x) + c_1(x) D_x + c_2(x) D_x^2 + \cdots + c_r(x) D_x^r\bigr)\cdot f \;=\; D_y\bigl(Q\cdot f\bigr),$$
and, when such data exist, outputs a tuple $(c_0,\dots,c_r)$ realizing the equality (a telescoper for $f$ with respect to $y$). The algorithm should be reduction-based, meaning it proceeds by constructing a $C(x)$-linear normal-form map on the relevant residue/quotient space modulo $D_y$-images so that telescopers are detected as $C(x)$-linear dependencies among the normal forms of $D_x^i \cdot f$, without explicitly computing the certificate $Q$.
artifact.status_search_result: A reduction-based creative telescoping algorithm for Fuchsian D-finite functions (with real exponents at singularities) was given by Chen, van Hoeij, Kauers, and Koutschan (ISSAC 2016 / JSC 2018), generalizing Trager's Hermite reduction. Subsequent work (e.g., Hermite reduction for D-finite functions via integral bases, 2023; reduction-based telescoping for definite summation of D-finite functions, JSC 2024) extends the approach to general D-finite functions.

status_evidence.title: Reduction-Based Creative Telescoping for Fuchsian D-finite Functions
status_evidence.snippet: We develop a reduction-based creative telescoping algorithm for fuchsian D-finite functions, generalizing the algorithm for algebraic functions to this larger class.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of designing such a reduction-based algorithm for Fuchsian D-finite functions has been solved.

status_evidence.title: Reduction-based creative telescoping for fuchsian D-finite functions - JSC
status_evidence.snippet: Journal of Symbolic Computation publication implementing the reduction-based telescoping algorithm for Fuchsian D-finite functions.
status_evidence.claim: Published journal version confirming the algorithm exists.

status_evidence.title: Reduction-based creative telescoping for definite summation of D-finite functions
status_evidence.snippet: Extends reduction-based creative telescoping beyond the Fuchsian case.
status_evidence.claim: Further generalization to D-finite functions has appeared.
